statement: Define an array b (with len(b) = len(nums)) to be obtainable from nums if there is a finite sequence of arrays a_0, ..., a_k of length len(nums) such that a_0 = nums, a_k = b, and for each t with 0 <= t < k, a_{t+1} is obtained from a_t by swapping the entries at some indices p and q with 0 <= p < len(nums), 0 <= q < len(nums), and |a_t[p] - a_t[q]| <= limit. Whenever the function returns a result r, r is obtainable from nums, and for every array b obtainable from nums, r is lexicographically no larger than b: either r = b, or at the least index h with 0 <= h < len(nums) and r[h] != b[h], we have r[h] < b[h].
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; 0 <= limit <= 1000000000.

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r; it does not fail through arithmetic overflow, out-of-bounds access, or panic.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; 0 <= limit <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, len(r) = len(nums).
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; 0 <= limit <= 1000000000.

statement: Let G be the graph whose vertices are the indices 0, ..., len(nums)-1, with an edge between two distinct indices p and q exactly when |nums[p] - nums[q]| <= limit. Whenever the function returns a result r, for every connected component C of G and every integer v, the number of indices i in C with r[i] = v equals the number of indices i in C with nums[i] = v.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; 0 <= limit <= 1000000000.

statement: Let G be the graph whose vertices are the indices 0, ..., len(nums)-1, with an edge between two distinct indices p and q exactly when |nums[p] - nums[q]| <= limit. Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i and j with 0 <= i < j < len(nums), if i and j are in the same connected component of G, then r[i] <= r[j].
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; 0 <= limit <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), min_{0 <= t < len(nums)} nums[t] <= r[i] <= max_{0 <= t < len(nums)} nums[t]. In particular, 1 <= r[i] <= 1000000000.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; 0 <= limit <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r[i] = nums[i] for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums).
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; limit = 0.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r is a nondecreasing permutation of nums: for every i and j with 0 <= i < j < len(nums), r[i] <= r[j], and for every integer v, the number of indices i with r[i] = v equals the number of indices i with nums[i] = v.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; 0 <= limit <= 1000000000; max_{0 <= t < len(nums)} nums[t] - min_{0 <= t < len(nums)} nums[t] <= limit.

statement: Let G be the graph whose vertices are the indices 0, ..., len(nums)-1, with an edge between two distinct indices p and q exactly when |nums[p] - nums[q]| <= limit. Whenever the function returns a result r, for every connected component C of G, if p is the smallest index in C, then r[p] = min_{i in C} nums[i].
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; 0 <= limit <= 1000000000.

statement: Let G be the graph whose vertices are the indices 0, ..., len(nums)-1, with an edge between two distinct indices p and q exactly when |nums[p] - nums[q]| <= limit. Whenever the function returns a result r, for every connected component C of G, if q is the largest index in C, then r[q] = max_{i in C} nums[i].
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; 0 <= limit <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every integer v, the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and r[i] = v equals the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] = v.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; 0 <= limit <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every index k with 0 <= k < len(nums) such that for all j with 0 <= j < len(nums) and j != k we have |nums[k] - nums[j]| > limit, it holds that r[k] = nums[k].
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; 0 <= limit <= 1000000000.
